editorial:
If you loved the first film, this sequel brings Gru back as a dad and former villain recruited by the Anti-Villain League to stop a new threat. A mysterious bad guy steals a serum that turns cute creatures into purple monsters, while Gru balances spy work, parenting, and a possible romance with agent Lucy Wilde. The Minions steal scenes with silly jokes, Gru's daughters still bring heart, and the whole movie keeps a bright, family-friendly energy.

The voice cast keeps things lively, the action moves fast, and the animation looks colorful and smooth. You get plenty of laughs, though the villain is less memorable and some story beats feel familiar. The pacing rarely drags, and the Minion scenes keep younger viewers entertained. It is a great pick for families, kids, and anyone wanting light fun. You can stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Gru and Lucy track the villain to his lair and discover he is actually El Macho, who faked his death. He uses the stolen serum to turn himself and his Minions into giant purple monsters. Gru and Lucy fight through the chaos, and Gru's love for his daughters helps him stay brave. Lucy saves Gru, they defeat El Macho, and the movie ends with Gru and Lucy getting married while the Minions celebrate.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves animated family comedies with silly humor and heart.
